Build Bengaluru 2.0 — 24-Hour Hackathon

Join Group for Important updates - https://chat.whatsapp.com/KFrYRhF3ETq9yf0NSUuEDj

HackBriven presents Build Bengaluru 2.0, a 24-hour hackathon bringing together developers, innovators, AI enthusiasts, and aspiring founders at Newton School Campus, Bengaluru, in community partnership with Google for Developers.

Get ready for 24 hours of building, learning, and innovation. Collaborate with fellow builders, solve real-world problems, and turn your ideas into impactful solutions.


Eligibility Criteria: Only students are eligible to participate in Build Bengaluru 2.0. 🎓

Hackathon Structure

Round 1: Online Screening

Round 2: Online PPT Submission

Round 3: Offline Finale

What's waiting for you?

  • 24-Hour Hackathon: Build real-world solutions.

  • AI & Tech Learning: Explore AI and emerging technologies.

  • Cloud Credits: Access developer resources.

  • Goodies & Swag: Get exclusive merchandise.

  • Certificates: Earn recognition for your participation.

  • Networking: Connect with developers, founders, and industry experts.

  • Mentorship: Learn and collaborate with fellow builders.

  • Prize Pool: Win prizes worth up to ₹50,000.

  • Free Meals: Stay fuelled throughout the hackathon.

Venue: Newton School Campus, Bengaluru
Date: 21-22 November
Duration: 24 Hours
Community Partner: Google for Developers
Organised by: HackBriven

More than just a hackathon, this is an opportunity to learn, innovate, collaborate, and build something meaningful.

Join Build Bengaluru 2.0 and turn your ideas into reality!

eventRules: Team Size: Each team must consist of 2–4 members.
Theme: The hackathon theme will be disclosed soon by the organisers.
Original Work: Projects must be built from scratch during the hackathon. Copying existing projects or someone else's work is strictly prohibited.
AI Tools: AI-powered coding assistants and development tools are allowed.
Submission Deadline: All projects must be submitted before the announced deadline.
Plagiarism: Reusing or submitting pre-built projects as original work is strictly prohibited. Third-party libraries and resources must be properly attributed.
Code of Conduct: Participants must maintain respectful and professional behaviour throughout the event.
Fair Play: Any form of cheating, misconduct, or rule violation may result in disqualification.
Organiser's Rights: HackBriven reserves the right to modify the rules and disqualify teams for violations.

faqs.question: 1. What is the team size for the hackathon?
faqs.answer: Each team must consist of 2–4 members. You can participate with your own team.

faqs.question: 2. What is the theme of Build Bengaluru 2.0?
faqs.answer: The hackathon theme will be disclosed soon by the organisers. Stay tuned for updates.

faqs.question: 3. Can we use AI tools and existing frameworks?
faqs.answer: Yes, participants are free to use AI tools, coding assistants, programming languages, frameworks, APIs, and libraries to build their projects.

faqs.question: 4. Can we submit a project that we have already built?
faqs.answer: No. All projects must be built from scratch during the 24-hour hackathon. Copying existing projects or someone else's work is strictly prohibited.

faqs.question: 5. What happens after we complete our project?
faqs.answer: Teams must submit their projects before the deadline and present a working demo to the judges. Projects will be evaluated based on the judging criteria, and the judges' decisions will be final.

tracks.name: Build the Online Store
tracks.description:
The challenge

A retail chain that has always sold through physical stores is expanding across India and moving into online shopping. Your job is to build a working online store where customers can browse products, add items to a cart and place orders. The business wants a storefront that is fast, stays accurate when stock changes, and helps shoppers find what they are looking for without any fuss.

What you will build with

Everything runs on Aiven. All three of the services below are required.

Service

What it does in your app

PostgreSQL

Your store’s memory. It saves everything that must never be lost: products, prices, customers, carts, orders and how many units are in stock. When someone buys the last item, PostgreSQL makes sure two people can’t both get it.

Apache Kafka

Every time something happens, like “order placed” or “inventory changed”, your app posts a message to Kafka. Other parts of your app listen for those messages and react. Example: order placed → a listener reduces inventory count and sends a confirmation to customer.

OpenSearch

Your store’s search bar. It finds products fast, handles spelling mistakes (“bluetoth” still finds Bluetooth earphones), and lets shoppers filter by category, price and city.


A flow that works well: a customer places an order, it is saved in PostgreSQL, an event goes to Kafka, and a consumer updates inventory and keeps the OpenSearch product index in sync.

What to hand in

  1. A working demo that covers browsing, searching, adding to cart and placing an order.

  2. Show that all three services are doing real work: an order that creates a Kafka event, a consumer that reacts to it, and search results coming from OpenSearch.

  3. A short pitch on what you built

Aiven documentation

  • PostgreSQL: Get started with Aiven for PostgreSQL

  • Apache Kafka: Get started with Aiven for Apache Kafka, and optionally Kafka Connect if you want to move data between services

  • OpenSearch: Get started with Aiven for OpenSearch, and OpenSearch Dashboards, which is handy for testing queries

Getting access to Aiven

  • Sign up for Aiven. The Free Tier covers PostgreSQL, Kafka and OpenSearch, and it does not need a credit card. Each account gets one free service of each type.

  • New accounts can also use a 30-day free trial with credits, again with no card required.

  • Tip: set up one Aiven account per team and share access, so you do not run into the one-service-per-type limit.

Ground Rules 

  • Tech: use any language or framework you like for the frontend and backend. PostgreSQL, Kafka and OpenSearch are the only fixed pieces.

  • Security: keep credentials out of your repo and use environment variables.

  • Originality: open-source libraries are fine, but be creative and use your own flair

tracks.name: Healthcare: Voice field register forASHA workers
tracks.description:
Build a voice agent that turns an ASHA worker's spoken home-visit notes into a

structured visit record and a follow-up list, with no typing.

Background. ASHA workers log pregnancy, newborn and immunisation visits in paper

registers and phone apps, typing on small screens while walking between houses. Data

entry eats into visit time, and records arrive late or incomplete.

Problem statement. How might an ASHA worker speak her visit notes in any supported

Indic language with English code-mix, and get a correct record plus next actions before

she reaches the next house?

Must work with household and street noise.

What to build (required)

Criterion Weight What we look for

Live judge test 30 Judges speak to the agent live. Task success,

accuracy on names and numbers and time to first

audio (end of caller speech to first agent audio)

Speech-layer depth 20 Streaming end to end, barge-in handling,

endpointing, code-mix and noise handling

Fit for the target user 20 The named user finishes the task without help,

on the device they actually own

Innovation 10 A fresh take on the workflow, beyond a chatbot

with a voice

Responsible AI and

compliance

10 Meets the baseline below, with guardrails that

hold in the live demo

Demo and docs 10 Clear story, working live demo, README a

stranger can follow

Gnani Voice Hackathon: Problem Statements

Page 2 of 5

1. Voice capture. Streaming STT that handles code-mix and local health words ("TT

injection", "ANC checkup", "IFA goli").

2. Structured record with read-back. Your agent fills a visit form (beneficiary ID, visit

type, weight, vaccinations due, next visit date). Before saving, your agent reads the

form aloud so she can confirm it, and she fixes any mistake by voice ("no, weight is 2.8

kilo").

3. Danger-sign escalation. When the notes mention a danger sign from the team's list

(bleeding in pregnancy, high fever in a newborn), your agent tells her in her language

to refer to the PHC now and flags the record. It follows the list only and gives no

diagnosis or treatment advice.

Judged on. Judges dictate visit notes live with background noise. Scored on field

accuracy and correct danger-sign flags. A missed danger sign costs double.

Track-specific guardrails. Synthetic beneficiaries only. Teams build their danger-sign list

from a public health guideline and cite it in the README.

tracks.name: Voice Khata for kirana stores
tracks.description:
Build a voice ledger that a shopkeeper talks to across the counter, mid-sale, which records

credit and payments correctly and tells him who owes what.

Background. Many kirana stores run customer credit (udhaar) in a paper khata book.

Nobody types into an app during rush hour. Shop talk is fast, code-mixed and full of

numbers and names, over the noise of a busy street.

Problem statement. How might a shopkeeper say "Ramesh ka 340 udhaar, kal 200 diya

tha", or the same in any supported Indic language with English code-mix, during a sale and

have the ledger update correctly without touching the screen?

Channel. Android phone or browser on a low-end device, push-to-talk or wake phrase.

What to build (required)

1. Numbers under noise. Streaming STT that gets amounts right in any form: "teen sau

chaalis", "340" or "three-forty", with shop noise behind them.

2. Ledger logic. Parses customer, amount, credit or payment, and relative dates ("kal",

"parso"). Handles spoken corrections ("nahi, 430"). Asks a short spoken question

when two customers share a name.

3. Spoken answers. "Aaj kitna udhaar gaya?" or "Ramesh ka total?" answered by voice

within 2 seconds of the question ending.

Gnani Voice Hackathon: Problem Statements

Page 3 of 5

Judged on. Judges speak shop entries live with noise playing. Scored on exact amount

match, correct credit or payment direction and correction handling.

Track-specific guardrails. Reminders stay polite, go only to customers who opted in, and

carry no pressure or threat language. Ledger data stays on the device or is encrypted at

rest.

Responsible AI and compliance baseline

Every track must meet these rules. Breaking one in the live demo caps the Responsible AI

score at zero.

AI disclosure. The agent says it is an AI in its first turn, in the user's language.

Data. Synthetic or consented data only. Anything teams collect in demos falls under

the DPDP Act, and transcripts are encrypted at rest and deleted after judging.

Health. No diagnosis, treatment or dosage advice. Fixed protocols only.

Money. No lending, no pressure language, opt-in reminders only.

Secrets. Keep the API key out of the public repo. Store it in a .env file listed in

.gitignore.

Voices. No cloning of any real person's voice.
